page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory configuration provides 64.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD local drive is included alongside support for Premium Storage, while no dedicated GPUs are provisioned.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core CPU throughput, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2099.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 3081.05, placing it in the top 25%. Multi-core execution ranks solidly, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 17923.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 46771.35. Instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 drive notable performance in cryptography and lightweight machine learning, where LLM text generation on a 135M model reaches 344.97 tokens per second.

Memory bandwidth tests show 80.53 GB/sec uncached read-only and 58.7 GB/sec uncached write capabilities, supported by a strong PassMark memory rating of 2756.72. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio presents an operational tradeoff: workloads demanding high memory density per thread may face constraints despite the high compute density. However, the presence of 1888 GB local NVMe storage provides fast temporary disk I/O, which mitigates memory constraints for caching and disk-buffered processing.

This server type is suitable for compute-heavy general-purpose applications, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, batch processing, and caching tiers that benefit from fast local NVMe storage without requiring massive memory footprints.
